segments.english: Serug lived thirty years, and he fathered Nahor.
segments.literal: and-lived Serug thirty year and-fathered [object-mark] Nahor

tokens.note: wayyiqtol: narrative past; the verb of the chronology formula

phrases.literal: 'and-lived Serug thirty year'; singular שָׁנָה after a decade number

grammar: וַיְחִי and וַיּוֹלֶד are wayyiqtols that carry the genealogy forward.
The etnaḥta on שָׁנָה divides the verse: age, then the birth.
The noun שָׁנָה stays singular after שְׁלֹשִׁים, as after tens in general.
segments.note: Names follow decisions.md: Serug, Nahor. הוֹלִיד is rendered 'fathered'.

commentary.summary: Onkelos renders the verse closely with וַחֲיָא ... וְאוֹלִיד, agreeing with the plain sense.

segments.english: Serug lived, after he fathered Nahor, two hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
segments.literal: and-lived Serug after his-fathering [object-mark] Nahor two-hundred year and-fathered sons and-daughters

tokens.note: wayyiqtol: narrative past; the verb of the chronology formula
dual form מָאתַיִם: 'two hundred'; the lexicon lists only the sense 'hundredth' under מֵאָה

phrases.literal: 'after his-fathering [object-mark] Nahor'; English finite clause for the infinitive

phrases.english: and he fathered sons and daughters

grammar: אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ is a temporal phrase: preposition plus infinitive construct with suffix.
The English keeps the Hebrew order, with 'after he fathered Nahor' set inside the age statement.
בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת, 'sons and daughters', is a formula closing each life.
segments.note: The English keeps Hebrew order so that the phrases stay in sequence; the sense is 'Serug lived two hundred years after he fathered Nahor'.

commentary.summary: Onkelos has בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד, 'after he fathered', the same sense.

segments.english: Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and he fathered Terah.
segments.literal: and-lived Nahor nine and-twenty year and-fathered [object-mark] Terah

tokens.note: wayyiqtol: narrative past; the verb of the chronology formula

phrases.literal: 'and-lived Nahor nine and-twenty year'; units precede tens

grammar: Hebrew puts the units first: תֵּשַׁע וְעֶשְׂרִים, 'nine and twenty'.
תֵּשַׁע is feminine to agree with שָׁנָה.
The zaqef qaton on נָחוֹר sets off the subject.
segments.note: Terah is the form fixed in decisions.md; the lexicon spells it Tarah.

commentary.summary: Onkelos has עֶשְׂרִין וּתְשַׁע שְׁנִין, the same number.

segments.english: Nahor lived, after he fathered Terah, one hundred nineteen years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
segments.literal: and-lived Nahor after his-fathering [object-mark] Terah nineteen year and-hundred-of year and-fathered sons and-daughters

tokens.note: wayyiqtol: narrative past; the verb of the chronology formula
construct מְאַת; the lexicon lists only the sense 'hundredth' under מֵאָה

phrases.literal: 'nineteen year and-hundred-of year'; Hebrew puts the smaller number first

phrases.english: and he fathered sons and daughters

grammar: תְּשַׁע־עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וּמְאַת שָׁנָה is 'nineteen years and a hundred years', that is 119.
The maqqef joins תְּשַׁע to עֶשְׂרֵה as one number.
The English keeps Hebrew order; the sense is 'Nahor lived 119 years after he fathered Terah'.
Each verse of the genealogy ends in the formula 'sons and daughters'.
segments.note: Numbers are given in words per decisions.md.

commentary.summary: Onkelos has מְאָה וּתְשַׁע עֲשַׂר שְׁנִין, the same number, 119.
